description: national: the CONUS EPA AQS formaldehyde monitors of the national analysis (24 h, 8 h and 3 h samples, Colorado included); colorado_24h: the seven Colorado 24 h sites of the case study; colorado_3h: the Colorado 3 h ozone-precursor sites (Chatfield State Park, Platteville). A Colorado sample can therefore appear in both a Colorado arm and the national arm.
EPA AQS site ID (state-county-site).
CDPHE site code (Colorado arms only).
Site name: AQS's for the national arm, CDPHE's for the Colorado arms (they can differ for the same station).
U.S. state.
County (national arm only).
AQS monitoring networks, e.g. NATTS, PAMS (national arm only; blank when AQS lists none).
Monitor latitude.
Monitor longitude.
Sampling duration.
Start of the sampling window.
End of the sampling window (start_utc + duration_h).
Local standard-time date on which sampling began.
Surface formaldehyde as reported to AQS, at 25 C and 1 atm; values reported in ppb (ppbC) were converted at 25 C and 1 atm. Collocated monitors (POCs) for the same window are averaged.
hcho_ugm3 as a mixing ratio (x 24.45 / 30.026).
Surface number density: hcho_ppb at the HRRR temperature and pressure averaged over the sampling window.
Number of collocated monitors (POCs) averaged (national arm only).
AQS qualifiers: code and description for the national arm, codes only for the Colorado arms. Samples with AQS null-data qualifiers were removed.
AQS sampling and analysis method (national arm only).
AQS sampling frequency (national arm only).
NOAA HRRR 2 m temperature averaged over the hours of the sampling window.
NOAA HRRR surface pressure averaged over the hours of the sampling window.
NOAA HRRR planetary boundary layer height averaged over the hours of the sampling window.
Share of the sampling window's hours with an HRRR analysis.
Shift of the TEMPO window relative to the sampling window (0 = the sampling window itself; national sub-daily samples -3, 0, 3; Colorado 3 h -3 to 9; 24 h samples 0 only).
TEMPO screen: maximum effective cloud fraction of a pixel (0.1, 0.2 or 0.3; primary 0.2).
TEMPO pixel block averaged around the monitor: 1x1, 3x3 or 5x5 pixels (primary 3x3).
Which TEMPO scans were used: those in the sampling window (shifted by lag_h), or, for a second Colorado 24 h variant, only those between 10:00 and 14:00 local standard time.
Start of the TEMPO window. A scan is assigned to the UTC hour containing its mid-scan time, and the scans whose hours fall in [tempo_start_utc, tempo_end_utc) are averaged.
End of the TEMPO window.
TEMPO scans with data over the site in the TEMPO window.
Scans in which at least half of the block's pixels pass the screen (main data quality flag 0, effective cloud fraction <= max_ecf, and the solar zenith angle and snow/ice limits in R/00_config.R).
TEMPO L3 V04 HCHO vertical column: mean over valid scans of each scan's mean over the passing pixels of the block.
Boundary-layer height supplied with the TEMPO retrieval, mean over valid scans.
Surface pressure supplied with the TEMPO retrieval, mean over valid scans.
Space-separated start of the UTC hour of each valid scan.
Effective mixing height: tempo_vc / hcho_molec_cm3 / 1e5.
TRUE when the sample has both a surface value and a TEMPO column (at least one valid scan).
TRUE when NOAA Hazard Mapping System smoke files exist for every day the window touches; the smoke columns are blank otherwise.
HMS smoke polygons over the site whose analysis period overlaps the sampling window widened by 3 h on each side.
Densest of those polygons: 0 none, 1 light, 2 medium, 3 heavy.
none, light or medium/heavy, from smoke_max_density.
TRUE when smoke_max_density > 0.
TRUE when any HMS polygon covered the site on the window's HMS days, whatever its analysis period.
